newsitem.title: HAITI: Dominican Republic again deports Haitians.
newsitem.headline: Dominican Republic again deports Haitians.

text.p: Dominican authorities have resumed forced deportations of Haitians despite an amnesty agreement reached between Haitian President Rene Preval and Dominican President Leonel Fernandez, authorities said on Friday.

Officials at the International Office of Migration and Haiti's National Office on Migration said about 56 Haitians were brought to the border town of Ouanaminthe on Wednesday, and several others to the central border point of Malpasse.
"The repatriations are now simply taking place unofficially," said National Office on Migration Director Carol Joseph.

Following repeated protests by Haiti over alleged human rights violations, the two presidents whose countries share the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, agreed verbally last month to stop the deportations until an international organisation was brought in to monitor them.

Haitian officials had protested that many of those forced out of the Dominican Republic were not illegal aliens, but Dominican citizens of Haitian decent forced to leave the Spanish-speaking nation because of their dark skin colour. They added that many of those deported were treated violently by Dominican soldiers.
Dominican officials said the deportations -- some 14,000 people were forced out of the country in just two months -- were a legitimate exercise of national sovereignty.

Haiti and the Dominican Republic have a history of mutual antagonism, much of it focused on the Haitians who leave their impoverished nation to work in the Dominican sugar industry or other unskilled jobs.
